rules.description: Spring (long): the bar's low trades below the range low by at least a minimum distance and the bar closes back at or above that level. Mirrored, the short side is Grimes's upthrust at range resistance.
rules.pseudocode: level = lowest(low[1], rangeLookback); low[0] < level - minPenetrationAtr * atr(atrLength) AND close[0] >= level

complexity.reason: a one-bar-shifted window extreme, an ATR margin and two comparisons on the same bar; no persistent state

catalog_match.note: that rule CAPS the penetration (Brooks's one-tick trap); this FLOORS it. Opposite bounds on the same event, so neither is the other at any parameter, and Grimes is explicit that a token poke is a bad spring

rules.merge_notes: Nine restatements of one same-bar test. The window-extreme level beat G16-04/G16-18's swing pivot on mechanizability. G10-11 supplies the floor (Grimes: a few cents is too little) and 0.25 ATR; at 0 this degenerates to SmallBreakoutTrapReversal with its cap disabled. G01-11 is the upthrust side.

rules.description: The bar's low comes down to within an ATR fraction of the low of the N bars ending `lag` bars ago (long, buying support); mirrored, the high reaches the N-bar high for the short.
rules.pseudocode: low[lag] <= lowest(low[lag + 1], levelLookback) + tolAtr * atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: a shifted window extreme plus an ATR-scaled one-sided tolerance

catalog_match.note: SIDES EXCHANGED: that rule's long is the high reaching the recent HIGH (momentum read); Grimes buys the touch of the recent LOW (fade read). A placement cannot borrow the other side's condition, the DistanceAboveRecentLow / PullbackFromRecentHigh precedent. Also not NearMissLevelReversal, a two-sided tick band plus a close-up term

rules.merge_notes: Tolerance in ATR fractions, not ticks, per the corpus's standing level-tolerance decision. `lag` follows StrongTrendBar's convention and exists so G04-02's "touched one bar ago, now well away" is two placements rather than a composite.

rules.description: The bar's body is at least a multiple of the mean high-low range of the N bars before it - Grimes's strong-momentum rejection bar, the bar that closes back across a broken level.
rules.pseudocode: abs(close[0] - open[0]) > bodyMultiple * average(high[1] - low[1], lookback)

complexity.reason: one body measurement against a window mean that excludes the judged bar

catalog_match.note: that rule measures the body against the mean BODY of the prior window and requires a with-trend colour; this measures it against the mean RANGE, a much harder test at the same multiple, and is direction-agnostic. Nothing in the catalog compares a body to other bars' ranges

rules.merge_notes: The momentum half of Grimes's failure test, carried atomically so the template is two panes. Benchmark excludes bar 0, the LargeOutsideBar / BodyAboveAverageMultiple convention. Also a bar_anatomy candidate (secondary bucket); merged here because the failure test is this bucket's.

rules.description: The absolute net change in the close over the last N bars is below a multiple of ATR - no directional progress, the second half of Grimes's random-walk trading-range read.
rules.pseudocode: abs(close[0] - close[lookback]) < netAtr * atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: one lagged close difference against an ATR multiple

catalog_match.note: a TWO-SIDED band on the same lagged difference, which no negate toggle on the one-sided mirrored Momentum reaches, and scaled in ATR so it ports across instruments. Complements RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple: a slow one-sided drift is tight by that rule's envelope and wide by this one

rules.merge_notes: G04-10's containment half IS RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple at its own defaults (20 bars, 4.0 ATR), so only the net-progress half is new; the two AND in the pane to give Grimes's full range test. See the trading-range design decision.

rules.description: The N-bar range width has stayed below a multiple of ATR on each of the last K consecutive bars - a consolidation that has lasted markedly longer than the trend's usual pauses.
rules.pseudocode: all k in 0..consecutiveBars-1: (highest(high[k], rangeLookback) - lowest(low[k], rangeLookback)) <= rangeAtrMultiple * atr(atrLookback)

complexity.reason: a run of window-width tests; ONE current ATR read for the whole run, never a lagged read of WFSafe_AvgTrueRange, per QuietBarCountInWindow

catalog_match.note: that rule plus ONE new `consecutiveBars` input (the MomentumConsecutiveBars / StrongTrendBarRun precedent); at 1 it is exactly the existing rule

rules.merge_notes: Grimes states a RATIO (a consolidation three or four times the trend's usual five to eight bars); tracking prior consolidation lengths needs machinery no source describes, so the ratio is baked into a fixed minimum, 18 bars. See the consolidation-length design decision.

rules.description: The support level of a recent window sits within an ATR fraction of the support level of an older, longer window - Grimes's confluence, levels from two scales lining up at one price. Mirrored on the highs.
rules.pseudocode: abs(lowest(low[1], shortLookback) - lowest(low[shortLookback + 1], longLookback)) <= tolAtr * atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: two disjoint window extremes and an ATR-scaled distance

catalog_match.note: nothing in the catalog compares two levels to each other; NearAnyLevel ORs the distance from PRICE to three magnets

rules.merge_notes: The multi-timeframe read is two lookbacks on one series, per the standing convention. THE WINDOWS MUST NOT OVERLAP: a nested long window's low is at or below the short window's and the test fires trivially whenever the long low is recent, so the older window is offset by shortLookback, the ReversalShortOfPriorExtreme construction.

rules.description: The close `lag` bars ago is above the close `lag + lookback` bars ago - the direction of the leg that ran into the current window. Negated on the long side it is Grimes's accumulation read (a decline precedes a base); as written it is the distribution read.
rules.pseudocode: close[lag] > close[lag + lookback]

complexity.reason: one comparison of two lagged closes

catalog_match.note: ADD ONE INPUT, `lag`, to Momentum (default 0, which leaves every existing template unchanged); at lag 0 it is exactly that rule. The LaggedHigherHigh precedent for a lag input on a bar comparison

rules.merge_notes: G02-01's Wyckoff phase test is a three-way composite: its tightness half is RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple, its flat-average half is EmaFlat, and only the prior-leg-direction term is new. Three panes beat one composite, so only that term is carried. See the accumulation/distribution design decision.

rules.description: Each of the last `legs` confirmed swing lows is above the one before it (short: swing highs each below the one before) - successively smaller declines into a level.
rules.pseudocode: all k in 1..legs-1: swingLow(k) > swingLow(k + 1)

complexity.reason: needs the pivot scan and `legs` confirmed pivots held at once

catalog_match.note: that rule plus ONE new `legs` input; at legs 2 it is exactly that rule, which already carries the pivot scan, the -1 sentinel guard and the maxBarsBack window

rules.merge_notes: Not HigherLowCount, which counts ADJACENT BAR pairs at a fixed lag rather than structure. A third pivot slot is the only new machinery; the -1 sentinel guard must be a bool on the scan's bar index, never a price test, since back-adjusted futures can print -1.00.

rules.description: The position has been open N bars, is not yet near its first target, and price has gone nowhere since entry (the N-bar range is a small fraction of the initial risk) - Grimes's stall warning on a failure-test trade.
rules.pseudocode: ctx.BarsSinceEntry() >= stallBars AND ctx.OpenPositionProfit() < riskMultiple * stopDistance AND (highest(high, stallBars) - lowest(low, stallBars)) < stallFraction * stopDistance

complexity.reason: position state plus a window-width test; no pivots

catalog_match.note: that rule is bars plus a profit sign; this adds the range-contraction term. EXITS ARE ORed, so the conjunction cannot be built from two exit placements - the NumBarsIfProfitable precedent, which is why that rule exists at all

rules.merge_notes: No initial-risk accessor exists, so risk is a `stopDistance` parameter per the standing convention; the authoring pass must reconcile units, since OpenPositionProfit is dollars while the range term is price points. Secondary bucket exits_targets; kept here as the failure test's management leg.

rules.description: The close sits in the top fraction of the session's range so far (long, a strength read); mirrored, in the bottom fraction for the short.
rules.pseudocode: (close[0] - sessionLow(0)) >= strongFraction * (sessionHigh(0) - sessionLow(0))

complexity.reason: running session high/low accessors; written multiplied so a session whose high equals its low cannot divide by zero

catalog_match.note: SAME STATISTIC, OPPOSITE POLARITY: that rule's long is a close in the BOTTOM of the session range (the fade read), Grimes's is a close in the TOP (the strength read). Add ONE boolean input, `strengthMode`, that swaps the two sides; the negate toggle does not reach it

rules.merge_notes: Grimes's close-as-percent-of-day's-range at his own 80/20 thresholds. Presented in the book as a monitoring text graph rather than a trigger, but the quantity is a plain ratio of differences and passes the shift test. On a daily bar the session is the bar and it degenerates to CloseRangePosition.

rules.description: The session's opening price sits in the top fraction of the session's range so far (long); mirrored, in the bottom fraction for the short. Grimes's O%Rng.
rules.pseudocode: (sessionOpen(0) - sessionLow(0)) >= highFraction * (sessionHigh(0) - sessionLow(0))

complexity.reason: running session high/low plus the session's opening price held for the session

catalog_match.note: that rule bands the session open against the running LOW in ATRs and reads it as strength; this places it inside the session range as a fraction and reads the top as strength - a different tolerance basis AND the opposite polarity

rules.merge_notes: Two restatements of one glossary metric (G16-13 names it O%Rng). The book's full-session range is knowable only in hindsight, so the range-to-date is used, as G08-27 itself proposes. Written multiplied, never as a ratio.

rules.description: Successively higher confirmed swing lows press into a flat resistance level (two recent swing highs within an ATR fraction of each other) - Grimes's ascending triangle; mirrored, the descending triangle into flat support.
rules.pseudocode: all k in 1..legs-1: swingLow(k) > swingLow(k + 1); AND abs(swingHigh(1) - swingHigh(2)) <= levelTolAtr * atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: pivots on both series at once - a run of rising lows and a flat pair of highs

catalog_match.note: the catalog's only triangle is the broadening one, which needs BOTH series diverging; this needs one series rising into the other held flat. No catalog rule tests a flat pair of pivots

rules.merge_notes: Carried as a composite (depends_on_keys) although its two halves are separately meaningful, because LevelTouchCount's resistance reading sits on its SHORT side and a long placement cannot borrow it - the same side-assignment obstruction as LowTouchesRecentRangeLow. Inline the pivot scan, -1 sentinel guarded as a bar index.

rules.description: Grimes's named Failure Test (Wyckoff spring/upthrust, Sperandeo's 2B): a brief excursion beyond a level - at most a few bars closing past it - that ends with a strong-bodied bar closing back on the origin side. Enter on that close.
rules.pseudocode: someBar k in 1..maxBarsBeyond closed below lowest(low, rangeBars) as of bar k+1 AND close[0] > that level AND abs(close[0] - open[0]) > bodyMultiple * average(high[1] - low[1], lookback)

complexity.reason: FailedBreakoutReversal's per-candidate window loop plus a single-bar body test

catalog_match.note: that rule is the excursion-and-reclaim half; this adds the strong-momentum reclaim bar the book insists on

rules.merge_notes: REACHABLE AS TWO PANES - FailedBreakoutReversal AND BodyExceedsAverageBarRange, both direction-compatible - so it earns a file only as the book's named template tested verbatim, which is why the brief lists it. G06-13's stop, target and reentry legs live in other buckets; its stall exit is StalledPositionExit.

rules.description: Some bar within the last few bars CLOSED beyond the N-bar level and this bar closes back on the origin side - the excursion-and-reclaim trigger of the failure test.
rules.pseudocode: someBar k in 1..maxBarsBeyond: close[k] < lowest(low[k + 1], rangeBars) AND close[0] > that level

complexity.reason: a per-candidate window extreme inside a short loop

catalog_match.note: identical bars: that rule's failBars is this rule's maxBarsBeyond and its rangeBars this rule's

rules.merge_notes: Three restatements. G05-09's standalone bars-beyond counter IS the existing rule's failBars window. Book values for maxBarsBeyond disagree: 1 (ch. 6, same or following bar) against 2-3 (ch. 5 rule of thumb) - both are grid values. G05-19 is the same test with rangeBars at trend scale, 50.

rules.description: Within the last few bars the LOW traded below the N-bar level (no close required) and this bar closes back above it.
rules.pseudocode: someBar k in 1..reverseBars: low[k] < lowest(low[reverseBars + 1], rangeBars) AND close[0] > that level

complexity.reason: one fixed window extreme offset past the bars allowed to break it, plus a short scan

catalog_match.note: same bars: that rule's reverseBars loop over an intrabar low against a once-fixed window level, with a reclaim margin this pair does not state

rules.merge_notes: G07-28 is that rule at reverseBars 1 with a long lookback - its higher-timeframe range is a longer window, a grid value, not new machinery; StopRunReversalBar is the same bar plus a bull-body term. G03-25's consolidation low is the same window extreme.

rules.description: The close has moved at least a multiple of ATR away from the level that was tested a bar ago - Grimes's price rejection, the sign a level holds.
rules.pseudocode: low[1] <= lowest(low[2], levelLookback) + touchTolAtr * atr(atrLength) AND (close[0] - lowest(low[1], levelLookback)) > rejectionAtr * atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: two window extremes and two ATR-scaled distances

catalog_match.note: the rejection test itself IS that rule (the close at least K ATRs above the N-bar low, same side, same window basis). The "tested a bar ago" precondition is LowTouchesRecentRangeLow at lag 1, ANDed in the pane

rules.merge_notes: Grimes's contrast case (price grinding into a level with no rejection, which precedes a break) is BreakoutBase in breakouts.json, which carries G04-07 (this bucket's TightRangeNearLargerRangeEdge row folded into it at reconciliation - same four window extremes, same defaults). Nothing to author: the pair of placements covers it.

rules.description: The close sits just above the N-bar range low, inside a narrow band - buying the bottom of a well-defined trading range.
rules.pseudocode: rangeLow = lowest(low[1], rangeLookback); close[0] <= rangeLow + proximityAtr * atr(atrLength) AND close[0] > rangeLow

complexity.reason: a window extreme and an ATR band on the close

catalog_match.note: same side, same window: the close in the bottom fraction of the N-bar range. Only the band's basis differs - a fraction of the range height there, an ATR multiple here, and the corpus already carries both bases (NearAnyLevel uses ATR)

rules.merge_notes: Grimes himself flags this as the cleanest and rarest subset of support trades and points at the spring as the common, messier form, so the duplicate costs nothing.

rules.description: The level has been touched and held at least three times inside a lookback window. Grimes reads the count as evidence the level will BREAK, against the conventional view.
rules.pseudocode: touchCount(level, touchLookback, tolAtr) >= minTouches

complexity.reason: a touch counter against a held level

catalog_match.note: same counter, same defaults (40 bars, 3 touches). That rule's own notes already record BOTH readings - touches weaken the level or prove it - and leave the sign to the placement's direction and negate toggles, which is exactly Grimes's disagreement with the conventional wisdom

rules.merge_notes: G06-41's "tested cleanly without closing beyond" is the existing rule's breakTolAtr term; its minTests of 2 is a grid value against Grimes's own three-or-more in G04-06. Not TrendLineTouchCount, which counts touches of a sloping projected line.

rules.description: A level that price closed through is later retested from the other side and holds - broken resistance acting as support and the mirror.
rules.pseudocode: someBar k in 1..maxWaitBars closed above level AND high[0] >= level - retestTolAtr * atr(atrLength) AND close[0] > level

complexity.reason: the level must persist from the break to the retest

catalog_match.note: same bars: a close within maxWaitBars broke the level and this bar pulls back to it and holds, with a toleranceAtr band and a maxOvershootAtr cap. G04-04's long-labelled side (broken support becoming resistance) is that rule's short side

rules.merge_notes: This is the one rule in the bucket where the level genuinely must persist across time, so the existing rule's confirmed swing pivot - not a rolling window extreme - is the right level source. See the level design decision.

rules.description: The recent window's height is smaller than the height of the window immediately before it - converging range edges, a symmetrical triangle.
rules.pseudocode: (highest(high, n) - lowest(low, n)) < contractionMultiple * (highest(high[n], n) - lowest(low[n], n))

complexity.reason: two adjacent window envelopes compared

catalog_match.note: exactly that rule (two adjacent fixed-length windows, the second smaller by shrinkFraction). The ENVELOPE beats the miner's mean-bar-range spelling on faithfulness too: Grimes's claim is that the range's EDGES converge

rules.merge_notes: The mean-bar-range reading of the same idea is already TrueRangeAvgRatio negated, which the catalog records as the book form of volatility contraction. ChannelWidthConvergence, the candidate's guess, is the pivot-line version and a different rule.

rules.description: Each swing, up and down, is larger than the one before it - a widening range Grimes says to avoid trading.
rules.pseudocode: swingHigh(k) > swingHigh(k + 1) for k in 1..2 AND swingLow(k) < swingLow(k + 1) for k in 1..2

complexity.reason: pivots on both series with alternating direction and growing amplitude

catalog_match.note: exactly that rule - both sides pushing further out at once, at least minLegs confirmed pivots in the window, identical both sides because a broadening formation carries no direction

rules.merge_notes: Grimes wants it as a block (avoid or size down), which is the existing rule placed with the negate toggle, or a Switch placement.

rules.description: A very large bar in one direction and a similar one in the other direction fall close together - Grimes's warning that a directionless, triangle-like consolidation follows.
rules.pseudocode: within the last withinBars there is a bull bar and a bear bar each with range >= sizeMultiple * average(high - low, lookback) measured before that bar

complexity.reason: two large-bar tests of opposite colour inside a window

catalog_match.note: exactly that rule, including its reading (two opposite spikes close together usually resolve sideways) and its benchmark (the mean range of the bars BEFORE each candidate, not an ATR). OppositeLargeBarPair is the adjacent-bar form

rules.merge_notes: The candidate's coolOffBars (block entries for N bars after the pair) is not carried: the existing rule's withinBars window already keeps the signal alive for that long, so the cool-off is the same input read the other way.

rules.description: The bar's high-low range is a multiple of the mean range of the bars before it - Grimes's large bar, read both as a climax marker and as evidence the lower timeframe trended inside it.
rules.pseudocode: (high[0] - low[0]) > rangeMultiple * average(high[1] - low[1], lookback)

complexity.reason: one range against a window mean

catalog_match.note: that rule at window 1 is exactly this test, with the same exclusive benchmark so a huge bar cannot raise its own bar. Not BarRangeAboveStd (mean plus K standard deviations) and not BarRangeAtrMultiple (the WFSafe ATR, gaps included)

rules.merge_notes: Two restatements. G01-10's actual claim - that a large bar contains a lower-timeframe trend and a small bar a lower-timeframe range - cannot be checked from the bars the engine sees; only the size comparison survives, and that is already in the catalog. Book multiple 2.

dropped.reason: primitive, not a testable condition - it only names 'level = the N-bar extreme'; settled once in design_decisions as the level definition and consumed by every level rule in this bucket
composition of SpringWithMinimumPenetration + G04-12 (diagonal range aligned with the higher-timeframe trend, context_regime)
composition of NearAnyLevel + BodyBelowAtrFraction - a close near the level with a small body; both halves are catalog rules that AND in the pane, and Grimes grades the pattern low-conviction himself
composition of LowTouchesRecentRangeLow + CloseRangePosition - the tail term is exactly CloseRangePosition at threshold 0.5 on the same side, so two placements reach it

cross_bucket.note: reconciliation pass: this bucket's TightRangeNearLargerRangeEdge was the same test as breakouts' BreakoutBase to the character (same four window extremes, same defaults), so all five of its sources are folded into that row
as G04-07; the counted narrow-bars-near-the-level form lost to the nested-window height form there
as G04-07; one of the two nested-window statements that won
as G04-07; this is BreakoutBase with proximityFraction disabled
as G04-07; the breakout-base statement the breakouts bucket already cited

design_decisions.topic: What a support/resistance level is (Grimes gives no algorithm)
options: the N-bar window extreme over the one-bar-shifted series, Highest(High, N)[1] / Lowest(Low, N)[1]
the most recent CONFIRMED swing pivot of strength S
the boundary of a range defined by K-bar width over ATR
design_decisions.recommended: BOTH, by role, and this is already the corpus's own practice: the one-bar-shifted WINDOW EXTREME is the default for every same-bar or few-bar test (break, touch, reclaim, rejection, spring), because it needs no pivot scan and no confirmation lag - StopRunReversalBar, TouchOfRecentExtreme, NearMissLevelReversal, SmallBreakoutTrapReversal, FailedBreakoutBeyondExtreme and RangeHeightProjectionTarget all use it; the CONFIRMED SWING PIVOT of strength S is used only when the level must persist from one event to a later one (a break followed by a retest, or a counted set of touches), which is what BreakoutLevelRetest, LevelTouchCount, SwingPointTestHolds and SwingPivotTarget already do. The third option collapses into the first, since a range boundary IS the window extreme. Tolerance around a level is ALWAYS an ATR fraction (0.1-0.25 typical, 0.5 for magnets), never ticks or price points: MinMove/PriceScale are unregistered and the engine exposes no tick size. The window must exclude the bars allowed to break it (offset by 1, or by reverseBars where several bars may break).

design_decisions.topic: The trading-range test ('the market is in a range')
options: RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple, the N-bar envelope against K x ATR
envelope AND no net directional progress (Grimes's random-walk reading)
design_decisions.recommended: RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple at its existing defaults - 20 bars / 4.0 ATR reads 'in a trading range', 15 bars / 1.2 reads 'tight', negate for 'trending' - which the catalog already calls the corpus's canonical classification; AND the new NetMoveBelowAtrMultiple alongside it when Grimes's stronger random-walk reading is wanted, since a slow one-sided drift is tight by the envelope and wide by net progress. Not ADX (the catalog records that it sits low inside such a drift). TradingRangeDay stays the session-scoped sibling for intraday work.

design_decisions.topic: Accumulation vs distribution (the Wyckoff phase test)
options: one composite rule: tight range AND flat moving average AND prior-leg direction
do not mechanize the phase at all
design_decisions.recommended: three panes. Two of the three halves already exist - RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple and EmaFlat - so only the discriminator is new, and it is one lagged close comparison: accumulation is a base with a DECLINE behind it (long context), distribution a base with an ADVANCE behind it (short context). Carry it as one new `lag` input on Momentum (PriorLegDirection). Do not author the composite.

design_decisions.topic: Consolidation length (how long a pause has lasted)
options: a run of consecutive bars on which the N-bar range width stays below K x ATR
a detector that measures each consolidation and remembers the trend's typical length
a longer rangeLookback at the same ATR multiple
design_decisions.recommended: the consecutive-bar run - one new `consecutiveBars` input on RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple (the MomentumConsecutiveBars precedent). Grimes states a RATIO ('three or four times the normal five to eight bars') and the history of prior consolidation lengths needed for a ratio is machinery no source describes, so bake the ratio into a fixed minimum of about 18 bars and let the grid move it. ONE current ATR read for the whole run, never a lagged read of WFSafe_AvgTrueRange.

design_decisions.topic: Spring/upthrust penetration bound: floor or cap
options: Grimes's floor (the poke must be decisive)
one rule with a two-sided band
design_decisions.recommended: keep both as separate files and let the data decide - they are opposite bounds on the same bar and the two books flatly disagree, which is worth testing. Keep spring and upthrust as ONE mirrored rule: no source in this bucket gives an asymmetric test, and G16-18's own note says the short side IS the upthrust.

design_decisions.topic: Side-assignment (polarity) when Grimes's long read is a catalog rule's short read
options: author a second file with the sides exchanged
add one boolean input to the existing rule that swaps its sides
treat it as a duplicate and rely on the negate toggle
design_decisions.recommended: NOT the third - the negate toggle gives 'not A', never the other side, and a placement carries one direction, so a fade rule and a momentum rule built on the same statistic are genuinely different rules (the catalog says so for DistanceAboveRecentLow vs PullbackFromRecentHigh). Author a second file when the rule carries real machinery (LowTouchesRecentRangeLow); add a boolean when the rule is a one-line ratio (CloseInTopOfSessionRange). Downstream buckets will hit this repeatedly on level, EMA and session rules.

bucket_summary: 47 candidates collapsed to 24 rules, 23 after the reconciliation pass folded TightRangeNearLargerRangeEdge into breakouts' identical BreakoutBase: the bucket was dominated by restatements of one same-bar spring/upthrust (nine candidates) and of the failure-test trigger (five more across two forms). The corpus already covers most of it - ten rules are catalog duplicates, chiefly FailedBreakoutReversal, FailedBreakoutBeyondExtreme, LevelTouchCount, BreakoutLevelRetest, ExpandingTrianglePattern and ShrinkingConsecutiveRanges. The A-list is twelve: the spring with a minimum penetration (Grimes's floor against Brooks's cap), the support-touch fade that the catalog only carries on the momentum side, the tight-range-at-the-range-edge base, the net-progress range test, and small parameterizations of Momentum, HigherSwingLow, RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple and the two session range-position rules. No candidate failed the shift test and nothing was sent to another bucket.
